analyst_view.overall: Early view: Brighton are second after a 1-0 win at Manchester City and a 2-0 home win over Brentford, while Newcastle are 12th under Matthias Jaissle and have won one of their last five. Brighton are also in the Champions League, so their squad will be stretched, and Newcastle face Arsenal first.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. I lean slightly lower: Brighton's last two league games were clean-sheet wins, 1-0 and 2-0, and Newcastle have scored only once in their last two league matches.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners. Brighton should have more of the ball at the Amex, but nothing in the news moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Brighton had four players booked against Brentford, though that was a heated game against ten men, and Newcastle had two late bookings at Fulham. I keep the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots, 17 of them Brighton's. That fits Brighton's control at home, but a Champions League week could bring some rotation, so I stay with the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Brighton are without Mitoma and Ferguson, which trims their threat a little, but Newcastle are short of bodies too with Livramento and Joelinton out. I stay with the site.
